credit: No confirmed portrait sourced for this archive.
bio: Walter Crane (1845–1915) was a British artist and book illustrator and an advocate of socialism and the Arts and Crafts movement. He also wrote occasional verse.
The poems here are taken from Arthur Quiller-Couch's anthology The Oxford Book of Victorian Verse (Clarendon Press, 1912).

poems.title: A Seat for Three: written on a Settle
poems.author: Walter Crane
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Victorian Verse (1912)
poems.text:
A seat for three, where host and guest
May side-by-side pass toast or jest;
And be their number two or three,
With elbow-room and liberty,
What need to wander east or west?
A book for thought, a nook for rest,
And, meet for fasting or for fest,
In fair and equal parts to be
A seat for three.

Then give you pleasant company,
For youth or elder shady tree;
A roof for council or sequest,
A corner in a homely nest;
Free, equal, and fraternally,
A seat for three.
